title: UiInterfaceMap
description: Complete map of a user interface: the composition tree, where each element sits, and how elements interconnect. Canonical artifact for the ui.component-contracts, ui.information-architecture, ui.screen-inventory and ui.layout obligations. Structure and intent are declared; symbols, enumerations and uncoverage are derived from the implementation, and a declared node always wins over a derived one.

surface.description: The surface this map describes. Must match a surface in the state matrix.

platforms.description: Platforms this map is authoritative for. Geometry is per-platform; semantic placement is shared.

states_source.description: Path to the state matrix whose state vocabulary this map references.

tokens_source.description: Path to the design token set whose tokens this map references.

sources.description: Glob patterns the deriver reads. An empty list disables derivation for this map.

mode.description: `fill-gaps` adds nodes the declaration omits; `verify-only` reports them as findings without adding. Both fail on divergence between a declared and a derived node.

id.description: Unique within the map. Stable, because edges and impact reports name it.

kind.description: What the element is. Closed vocabulary so a renderer can style any map without discovering new kinds at runtime.

label.description: The text a user actually sees. Required for every kind that renders text; a component with no label is an omission, not a styling choice.

role.description: What the element is for, in the interface's own terms.

intent.description: The user need this element serves. Not a restatement of role.

size_classes.description: Size classes where this element exists at all. An element absent from a class is a deliberate reflow, not an accident.

states.description: States this element can be in, drawn from the state matrix vocabulary.

tokens.description: Design tokens this element paints with.

inputs.description: How the user operates this element: a chord, `pointer`, or `paste`. Mouse is never the only route.

origin.description: Set by the compiler, not by the author.

slot.description: Where the element sits, semantically. A terminal has no stable pixel geometry, so position is expressed as a region plus an order and an alignment; a platform that does have pixels may add geometry.

region.description: Region of the containing element this child occupies.

order.description: Position within the region. Distinct values make the layout order total, so two renderers cannot disagree.

weight.description: Relative share of the region when the parent divides space.

stack.description: How this element arranges its own children.

condition.description: When this element is present. Mutually exclusive siblings share a position only by declaring a condition; two unconditional siblings may not, because nothing would tell a renderer which to draw.

geometry.description: Optional pixel geometry, declared per platform and only where pixels are stable. Absent for terminal surfaces on purpose.

symbol.description: Code symbol implementing this element. Resolved against the repository unless status is not-implemented.

path.description: File the symbol lives in, when it is not discoverable by name.

evidence.description: Golden frame, snapshot or test proving this element renders.

status.description: `not-implemented` is how the map describes a planned element without claiming it exists.

absent_reason.description: Required when status is not-implemented: why the element is described but not built.

edge.description: A non-hierarchical interconnection between two elements. The tree carries composition; edges carry everything that would be lost if it were forced into the tree: focus order, data flow, events, overlays and navigation.

label.description: What crosses the edge, in domain terms.

condition.description: When the edge is live, when it is not unconditional.
